newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - March 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - March 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Casablanca stock exchange has new headquarters and amended legislation to attract more investors.
- French-Italian firm SGS-Thomson has extended one of its two electronics plants in Casablanca; a second consortium shows interest in Casablanca subway.
- Moroccans do not lobby enough in European Union to promote products. They were absent from seminar on economic transition on March 20 and from recent textile fair in Brussels.
- State-owned tobacco company makes profits despite anti-smoking law, is one of main contributors to treasury with 5.65 billion dirhams ($607.5 million) in 1996.

- Since early January, Casablanca stock exchange has seen significant increases in stock values, boosted by shortage of shares and excess of money. Blue-chip stocks and mutual funds ensure stability, but small shareholders should realise that trading on bourse is not gambling but long-term investment.

- French consortium Bossard and Mazard commissioned to study ways to raise savings to 25 percent from current 19 percent; proposes action plan including broad reforms which old institutions might find difficult to undertake.
